note: Story-telling deck for Hermes Scrollback Reel. The facts of every episode come from the user's own gated history; this deck only decides HOW an episode is framed and drawn, so a new chapter never looks or reads like the last one. Combinations = conflicts x worlds x genres x villains x motifs x shots.

conflicts.label: a deadline that cannot be met as things stand
a fault nobody can see from the outside
a win that turns out not to count
the tool meant to check the work is itself wrong
two approaches racing for the same result
work that costs far more time than expected
the same failure returning again and again
something quietly breaking that used to work
records that disagree with each other
one strict check that almost nothing survives
a symptom far from its real cause
the fallback plan becoming the only plan

worlds.look: a citadel carved inside a humming mountain of servers, paper lanterns of streaming light
a flooded library of glass shelves, data drifting like kelp
an endless workshop of brass gears, half-built machines and hanging chains
a lighthouse in a permanent electric storm, cables arcing into black water
a city folded from paper and ink, streets that rearrange when nobody looks
an overgrown engine hall where vines grow through turbines
a desert of antennae and dead satellites under two moons
a lantern-lit market beneath a station, stalls of traded memories
a forge suspended between floating islands, sparks falling into cloud
a switchyard locked in ice, rails leading into fog
a cathedral that floods twice a day, choirs of blinking indicators
an after-hours office at 3am, screens the only light, coffee rings on every surface

genres.label: shonen duel: two wills colliding, impact frames, shouted resolve
noir procedural: rain, shadows, a case that keeps doubling back
quiet drama: small gestures, held silences, weight in the eyes
gothic mystery: candlelight, old machinery, something breathing in the walls
tournament arc: brackets, scoreboards, a rival with a signature move
heist: a plan with moving parts and one detail nobody accounted for
siege: holding a line while resources drain

villains.look: a towering clockwork figure with a stopped face and hands that reach too far
a two-faced phantom of glass shards, one face grinning, one weeping
a masked inspector whose stamp marks everything false, even true things
a many-armed creature made of identical broken copies of itself
a slow fog with teeth, unnoticed until it has already moved the walls
a colossal stone warden that lets almost nothing pass its gate
a bloated merchant of limits, weighing requests on a rusted scale
a creature wearing a borrowed shape, whispering that it has always been here
a ghost of a single decision, chained to the place it went wrong
a rider with two horses pulling opposite ways, unable to choose
a frost giant of rebooted machines, erasing warmth as it walks
an absence with weight: a chair, a shadow, a voice with no body

motifs.label: a blade drawn against a distant bell
a red thread tying scattered pieces together
a compass that points at the thing you fear
a mirror cracking along an old line
a paper boat setting out on dark water
a map burning from the corner inward
two doors, one opening onto the other
an open hand holding something small and important

shots.label: low angle on the hero, sky behind
close on hands and the object
high angle, figure small in the frame
